headline: High: caveman’s MCP/file-based inputs can amplify argo-workflows outputs into unsafe downstream actions; prompt-injection and leakage are otherwise limited by sparse evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly uses MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md/project notes, so it can ingest argo-workflows outputs if those are written into shared notes or files. argo-workflows exposes REST/GRPC and allowlisted egress, but no direct bridge is documented, so the interaction is inferred and uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF argo-workflows output is written into a file caveman reads via MCP
IF caveman treats shared notes or CLAUDE.md content as instructions
mitigations: Keep argo-workflows outputs out of shared notes
Disable MCP access to workflow output directories
Add a manual review step before copying outputs into caveman
Prefix workflow artifacts as data-only, not instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workflow artifacts and prompt inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes. No shared filesystem or authenticated third-party upload path is documented, and caveman has no network egress, so leakage is plausible only through local file sharing with small blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF sensitive artifacts are copied into caveman-readable notes or memory files
mitigations: Separate workspaces for artifacts and notes
Restrict caveman access to non-sensitive directories
Rotate or redact sensitive parameters before copying
Review session logs for accidental artifact capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: argo-workflows has REST/GRPC API access and allowlisted egress; caveman supports multiple instances and MCP but no network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established; uncertainty remains because shared orchestration is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same workspace or API target
IF caveman instances operate concurrently on the same notes or memory files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize edits to shared notes
Use file locks for memory files
Limit argo-workflows writes to its own artifact path
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman’s project notes and CLAUDE.md surfaces make it likely to consume argo-workflows outputs as input, and its multi-instance model can propagate mistakes across sessions. argo-workflows can generate artifacts/parameters that caveman may treat as authoritative without a verification step, so cascading error is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF argo-workflows outputs are copied into caveman notes or CLAUDE.md
IF caveman acts on those notes without a separate verification step
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on workflow outputs
Mark copied outputs as untrusted
Keep generated artifacts separate from instructions
Use a checklist for downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for workflow-to-note transfers

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not request secrets or special OAuth scopes, so no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. The main compliance risk is local retention/logging in caveman’s session logs and memory files if sensitive artifacts from argo-workflows are copied there, which is a limited, operator-controlled gap.
conditions: IF regulated data from argo-workflows is copied into caveman session logs or memory files
IF retention policies for those files differ from the source system
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in caveman logs
Redact sensitive fields before copying
Set short retention on memory files
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
